clue.text: Empty spaces V & A filled with insight, despatching men

indicators.note: despatching means sending away, so the named letters are sent out of the word
the two letters given first are filled, so the other piece goes between them

blocks.note: the two letters taken as written, as in the London museum's nickname
acumen is sharp insight
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Victoria and Albert Museum's galleries stand empty after the staff have been sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: The V & A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum; here it is simply two letters to be filled.
explanation.definitionFit: VACUA is the Latin plural of vacuum, so it names empty spaces in the plural.

clue.text: Going after notoriety (rumoured), German abused chit in local court once

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed by word of mouth, so the sound counts
something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape
going after means following, so the later pieces come after the first one

blocks.note: notoriety is fame of a kind
Ger. is the abbreviation for German
taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A German's notorious misuse of a note lands him in a local court of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vehmgericht was a secret tribunal of medieval Westphalia, a regional court long since gone.

clue.text: Site of Bowie's last stand in gala, momentous

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the words that follow, across their join

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: David Bowie's final concert was at a grand gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowie looks like the singer; it is Jim Bowie, who died defending the Texas mission in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in San Antonio is where Jim Bowie and the other defenders were killed by Mexican forces.

clue.text: Equine disease, onset of rickets in young one

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so the first letter is kept
one piece goes in the other, which surrounds it

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal
its first letter

explanation.surface: A foal goes down with rickets, a disease of horses.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes between CU and B.
explanation.definitionFit: A curb is a hard swelling on a horse's hind leg just below the hock, a recognised equine ailment.

clue.text: Cost of travel round Iran is a distant culmination for voyage

indicators.note: the culmination of something is its end, so the last letter is kept
the later pieces go round the other one, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
far means distant
its last letter
IR is Iran's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: The price of a long trip around Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: Round applies to the whole run that follows Iran, which splits after its first letter to take the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfare is the price paid for a flight, so it is a cost of travel.

clue.text: Fancy assistant No. 1 being demoted to No. 4

indicators.note: the letter in first place is moved down to fourth place, the rest moving up

blocks.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A top assistant is unexpectedly demoted down the pecking order.
explanation.walkthrough: The A at the head of AIDE drops to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim, which is a sense of idea.

clue.text: Producing what's central for charcuterie in sausage skin?

indicators.note: what is central to a word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept
one piece is placed in the other, which wraps around it

blocks.note: a sausage casing is its skin
the sixth of its eleven letters

explanation.surface: A question about what goes into a sausage at the delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside CASING after its first two letters, giving CA-U-SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing and producing are synonyms as verbs: both mean bringing about an effect.

clue.text: Sign most of fruit is in credit with sun rising

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter
what is in another word sits inside it
in a down clue a word rising reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit
an apricot is a fruit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horoscope note: fruit is in credit as the sun rises in your sign.
explanation.walkthrough: CR for credit is a standard abbreviation, and it splits around the shortened fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricornus is the Latin name of the constellation and zodiac sign Capricorn, the goat.

clue.text: Projectile launcher finally left, not having succeeded

indicators.note: not having something means lacking it, so the letter is removed

blocks.note: at last means finally
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An archer's weapon is finally abandoned, having failed.
explanation.walkthrough: AT LAST without its S gives ATLAT, followed by L.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlatl is the Aztec spear-thrower, a device for launching darts or javelins.

clue.text: Top scorer in pack once, and so made to ingest stuff, being poorly?

indicators.note: a word made to ingest others swallows them, holding them inside

blocks.note: taken as written
to pad is to stuff
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A top rugby scorer is force-fed and falls sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Pack looks like a rugby scrum; it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The spadillo was the ace of spades in ombre and quadrille, the highest trump in those old card games.

clue.text: Feeble fool in escapade I'll encourage, given a lift

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A weak fool joins a prank because someone promised encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A nellie, or nelly, is a weak, silly or effeminate person in British slang.

clue.text: Special forces shot Brent geese around edge of river (11, two words)

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter here

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
its first letter

explanation.surface: Commandos shoot wild geese beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Brent geese are small dark wild geese that winter on British coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Berets are the US Army Special Forces, named after their headgear.

clue.text: To explain dodgy clue I'll require day

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
a date is a particular day

explanation.surface: A solver admits needing a day to explain a tricky clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the I of I'll is wordplay; 'll require just joins it to the date that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make something clear, which is a synonym for explaining it.

clue.text: Dip on this prom becomes increasingly crazy

blocks.note: dippy means daft, and dippier is the comparative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaside paddle off the promenade is said to make bathers ever more unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: DIP placed on the answer makes DIPPIER, so the answer is what is left of DIPPIER once DIP is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists a promenade among the senses of pier, a structure walked along out over the sea.

clue.text: He has Moroccan tree planted within capital

indicators.note: a thing planted within something else is set down inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the arar is the sandarac tree of North Africa

explanation.walkthrough: The arar, or sandarac tree, is a crossword favourite drawn from Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Power up front, i.e. ball shifted? typical of pushover?

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: Up front says that P comes at the start, before the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is someone easily persuaded, and pliable means easily bent or influenced.

clue.text: Couplets? Here's very short one penned in Norfolk town

indicators.note: something penned in is shut inside an enclosure

blocks.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
tich, from the music-hall comic Little Tich, is a very small person

explanation.surface: A poet offers couplets about a short man confined to a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is a county in eastern England; Little Tich was a tiny Victorian music-hall comedian, hence tich for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A distich is a pair of verse lines, so distichs are couplets.

clue.text: Dance in line that has loafer tripping around also

indicators.note: a person tripping stumbles about, so these letters fall out of their order
the rearranged letters go around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
and, like also, adds one thing to another

explanation.surface: An idler stumbles round the floor in a line dance.
explanation.walkthrough: In line belongs to the definition: the dance is performed in a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The farandole is a Provençal folk dance in which the dancers hold hands in a long chain.

clue.text: Busily engaged? O, I dig on frantically at edges of fossilized mollusc

indicators.note: done frantically means done in a wild rush, so these letters end up in disorder
letters placed at the edges of something sit on both sides of it

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
someone at it is busily engaged

explanation.surface: A fossil hunter digs away frantically around a find.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase, read as an idiom, is AT IT; the anagram GONIOID is split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A goniatitoid is a member of an extinct group of ammonoids, shelled molluscs known only as fossils.

clue.text: Orcadian landowner producing decorative slab in gold

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, which encloses it

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
a dalle is a decorated tile or slab

explanation.surface: An Orkney landowner makes a slab set in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: DALLE goes between O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An odaller holds land by udal tenure, the old freehold system of Orkney and Shetland.

clue.text: Murray and suchlike, one following in G. Player's footsteps

definitions.note: read as E. Els, a name with its initial

blocks.note: second meaning: Ernie Els, the South African golfer who followed Gary Player

explanation.surface: Andy Murray and his kind are compared to a golfer following Gary Player.
explanation.walkthrough: Murray looks like the tennis player; it is the fish. Gary Player and Ernie Els are both South African golf champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Morays, also spelt murrays, are a family of eel, so they and their kind are eels.

clue.text: Tea cake, famously-short-lived: icer carelessly has left one in the middle

indicators.note: done carelessly means done sloppily, so the letters come out jumbled
the added letters are placed in the middle of the others

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for left
a means one

explanation.surface: A careless pastry cook leaves one cake half-iced at tea time.
explanation.walkthrough: Famously short-lived recalls Chambers' joke definition of the word: a cake long in shape but short in duration.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is an iced choux pastry served with tea, and so tempting that it never lasts long.

clue.text: Element in couplet central to poet, singly paired

indicators.note: what is central to a word is its middle, so only the inner letters are kept
one piece goes in the other, which surrounds it

a couplet is a pair, so the piece just built is written a second time

explanation.surface: A part of a rhyming couplet is said to be the heart of a poet's art.
explanation.walkthrough: Couplet is the unusual step: it doubles the result, so the answer is the same short word twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: One-one is the Chambers term for a one-to-one correspondence, each item matched singly with one partner.

clue.text: Latin book, including one that's not new in classical library

clue.text: Swimming in the sea, only tailless, unable to stand very salty water

clue.text: Ungenerous, that is without charge returned, recovers without lies

clue.text: Men will be involved with routine in this with nothing changing?

taken as written
